info.title: Darpan Facade API
info.description:
GENERATED from the facade service XML — do not edit by hand. Regenerate with ./gradlew :runtime:component:darpan:generateApiContract.

Transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 over POST /rpc/json. Auth channels: browser SPA uses the HttpOnly darpan_login_key cookie + CSRF token (canonical); integration callers and no-credentialed-CORS fallbacks use the login_key header (in-memory only, never query params). HTTP status is 200 for every dispatched call; distinguish outcomes by shape. JSON-RPC error object: protocol failures (-32700 parse, -32600 invalid request, -32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params), unhandled service errors (code 500), authorization denial (code 403). Facade business validation instead returns a success envelope with result.ok=false and result.errors[].

GetLiveOperationsParams.description:
DAR-ADMIN-008. What is running on this instance right now, across every tenant: each
            in-flight reconciliation, automation and audit run with its stage, progress and health, the
            automation slots and overdue schedule, failures in the last 24 hours, this JVM's load, and the
            warnings that follow, critical first.

            Run health compares a run with its own last successful run, because heartbeats tick only inside
            the extract stages: a long compare with a silent heartbeat is not stuck. System figures describe
            the one JVM that answered. A source that could not be read is listed in unavailable, never
            reported as zero. Rules: darpan.admin.LiveOperationsRules.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp — ISO-8601 string or epoch milliseconds

warnings.description:
severity (critical | warning), code, title, detail, tenantLabel, runResultId,
                        automationId, since. Critical first, then oldest first.

running.description:
One row per RUNNING run result: kind (audit | automation | run), name, tenant,
                        currentStage, progressPercent, startedDate, elapsedMs, usualDurationMs, health
                        (healthy | slow | stuck), healthReason.

overdue.description:
Active automations past their fire time by more than one scan tick and not
                        still running, latest first.

slots.description:
inFlight and cap (darpan.reconciliation.automation.maxConcurrentExecutions,
                        instance-wide), plus pending executions. DAR-BE-143, this instance's admission: queued (runs
                        waiting for a slot), perTenantCap, heldForMemory and holdAtHeapPercent, and byTenant
                        {tenantId: {running, queued}}.

recentFailures.description: windowHours, count and items: failed run results in the window, newest first.

system.description:
Heap, heap after GC, process CPU, load average, threads, disk on the runtime
                        volume, the Moqui worker pool and uptime. Null when unreadable.

unavailable.description: source and reason for each source that could not be read.

UpdateRetentionPeriodsParams.description:
Sets, for the instance or for one tenant, how long each table keeps its rows. periods maps a table key
            (AUDIT_FINDING, RUN_RESULT, AGENT_MESSAGE, AGENT_QUERY_LOG, SYNC_PULSE_SAMPLE) to a whole number of days from 1 to 3650, to forever, or (a
            tenant only) to inherit (drop the tenant's own period and follow the instance's). A tenant's own period, including forever,
            wins over the instance period for that tenant's rows only. Refused as a whole, with the reason and nothing saved: an
            unknown table, a value that is not one of those, inherit at instance level, an unknown tenant, forever at instance level
            while a JVM property pins the period, forever at instance level for a table whose period has a default
            (SYNC_PULSE_SAMPLE: removing the setting brings back its 30 days; a tenant's own period may still be forever). A table whose period does not change is skipped. While the retention job is running
            (not paused), a change that keeps rows for less time (a shorter period, or forever to days) needs previewedRows, the total
            dryRun#Retention showed for the same change: the preview is run again and the change is refused when today's count is more
            than 100 rows or 5% above it. Lengthening, and any change while the job is paused, needs no preview. Instance periods go
            through the settings store (one AdminAuditLog row per table, `key: old -> new (note)`); a tenant's go to its own
            TenantRetentionPeriod rows (one AdminAuditLog row for the call: `TABLE: before -> after`).

            the scanner owns. Later entries are projected from scheduleExpr and assume the automation is
            not paused, edited, or deferred by the concurrency cap before it gets there.

            scan_ReconciliationAutomations_5m (scanCron, default "0 0/5 * * * ?", editable with update#ServiceJob), because
            nothing is submitted between runs. While that job is paused (scanPaused) nothing is submitted: submitsAt and
            concurrentAtTick are empty. concurrentAtTick counts the fires sharing a run, to be read against
            inFlightCap (darpan.reconciliation.automation.maxConcurrentExecutions).

ResetServiceJobParams.description:
Puts a Darpan job back on its shipped defaults. With no parameterNames: the cron and pause state go back to the
            shipped ones, every parameter edited here goes back to its default (a parameter with no default is deleted), and the
            job follows the defaults on every later deploy again. With parameterNames: only those parameters (the cron and pause
            state stay edited). A reset that resumes a job with resumePreviewService needs previewedRows, as update#ServiceJob does,
            and a reset that changes the cron counts as a run made now, as there. A job already on its defaults changes nothing and
            writes no audit row. Writes one AdminAuditLog row naming each change.

UpdateServiceJobParams.description:
Edits a Darpan job: its cron, its pause state, its parameters, in one call; refused as a whole, with the reason and
            nothing saved, when any part is wrong. Refused: a job that is not Darpan's, a cron that does not parse, is blank,
            over 120 characters, never runs within 400 days or leaves a gap under the job's minIntervalMinutes, paused other than Y or N,
            a parameter the job's service does not take, a blank value or one that does not convert to the parameter's type (a
            Boolean takes true, false, Y or N).
            Resuming (Y to N) a job with resumePreviewService (retention) needs previewedRows, the total the preview showed: the
            preview is run again and the resume is refused when today's count is more than 100 rows or 5% above it. Pausing needs
            no preview. A resumed job runs within about a minute (the runner catches up a run that was due while it was paused),
            unless the same call changes its cron. A cron change counts as a run made now (ServiceJobRunLock.lastRunTime), so moving
            the time to one already past today does not fire the job at once and break its floor; the next run is the cron's next
            time. A value equal to the live one is not a change; no change writes no audit row. Writes one AdminAuditLog row
            (`cron: a -> b; paused: Y -> N (preview showed N rows, today's dry run counts M); name: a -> b`).

GetSqlQueryResultParams.description:
Run one read-only SQL statement on the read-only datasource (darpan_sql_readonly, a SELECT-only DB user)
            and return at most maxRows rows. The statement must start with SELECT, WITH, SHOW, EXPLAIN or DESCRIBE, holds no
            ';', no write or lock word and no secret column name; it runs read-only and is always rolled back, with a 30-second
            timeout. Secret columns come back masked; encrypted fields stay ciphertext. A fresh two-factor proof (adminCode or
            adminPasskeyAssertion) opens a 15-minute window for the caller (not sliding; signing out ends it); while it is open
            no proof is needed and one given is not spent. Every call, refused or not, writes an AdminAuditLog row (in its own
            transaction, so it survives the query's rollback). Codes: SQL_READONLY_NOT_CONFIGURED, SQL_REFUSED,
            SQL_WINDOW_CLOSED, a TwoFactorRefusal name (CODE, PASSKEY, NOT_ENROLLED, ...), SQL_TIMEOUT, SQL_FAILED.

Restores one of the active tenant's config versions by applying exactly the plan preview#TenantConfigRestore
            showed: the current config is kept as a version first ("Before restoring version N"), then the restore is
            written and kept as a version ("Restored version N"). One transaction: all of it or none of it. Needs edit
            access to the tenant.

before.description:
The version kept before the restore (the version itself when nothing
                changed since it).

after.description:
The version the restore left (the same as before when the restore
                changed nothing).

plan.description: The plan applied, as preview#TenantConfigRestore answered it.

RestoreTenantConfigVersionResponse.description: JSON-RPC success envelope for facade.TenantConfigFacadeServices.restore#TenantConfigVersion. Check result.ok / result.errors for business failures.

SnapshotTenantConfigParams.description:
Keeps the active tenant's audit config as a new version when it changed since the latest one. Needs
            edit access to the tenant.

created.description: False when nothing changed; version is then the latest.

version.description:
{id, seq, parentId, hash, bundleVersion, counts: {audits, statements,
                checks, runs, queries, conclusionCodes, connections}, changeSource, reason, createdBy, createdDate}

CreateTenantQueryProposalParams.description:
A query proposed for the active tenant (by the agent or a person): its read is checked against
            get#TenantQueryCatalog and, when every source and field is in it, the query runs on the tenant's data so its
            result can be shown first. Nothing is saved; accepting it is save#TenantQuery. status: PROPOSED or REFUSED (code
            NOT_KEPT, UNKNOWN_SOURCE or INVALID_READ, with the field). Needs edit access.
